chunks: And in the narration of ʿAbdullāh ibn Maymūn, from Abī ʿAbdillāh, from his father, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, he said:

The adulterer has six traits: three in this world and three in the Hereafter. As for those in this world, he loses the light of the face, brings about poverty, and hastens destruction. And as for those in the Hereafter, they are the wrath of the Lord, an evil reckoning, and abiding forever in the Fire.

key_terms.خِصَالٍ: traits or consequences mentioned for a person
key_terms.نُورِ ٱلْوَجْهِ: the brightness or light of the face, meaning visible honor and grace
key_terms.ٱلزَّانِي: the adulterer; the one who commits zinā

ai.seo_question: What consequences does this hadith mention for adultery in this world and the Hereafter?
ai.summary: This hadith warns that zinā brings both worldly and otherworldly consequences. In this world it removes honor and blessing, while in the Hereafter it leads to divine wrath, severe reckoning, and punishment in the Fire.
